title: Geometric coroot characterized by the local normalizer reflection
statement: Let $F$ be a field and let $T,G$ be $F$-group schemes, $i:T\to G$ a group-scheme homomorphism, $\alpha\in X^*(T)$ a character and $c\in X_*(T)$ a cocharacter, with characters, cocharacters, point images and universal normalizers as in [def-sfb-rank-one-root-interfaces]. Define $\operatorname{IsGeometricCoroot}(i,\alpha,c)$ by the following conditions. The character $\alpha$ is nontrivial and $\alpha\circ c(s)=s^2$. There exists a largest subtorus $S\hookrightarrow\ker\alpha$ in the sense of [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], and a rational point $n\in N_G(i(T))(F)\setminus i(T)(F)$ which centralizes $i(S)$ scheme-theoretically, using the scalar-extension centralizer condition of [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. For every character $\chi$ there is an integer $m$ with $\chi\circ c(s)=s^m$, and for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $t\in T(A)$ there is $t^{\prime}\in T(A)$ with $i(t^{\prime})=n^{-1}i(t)n$ and $\chi(t^{\prime})=\chi(t)\alpha(t)^{-m}$. For a root of a split reductive pair this specifies its geometric coroot by the nonidentity Weyl reflection in $C_G(S)$, including its central-torus component.
